historical_record.description: The Recreation and Park Commission approved a mural, funded through the Mural Resource Center and already approved by the Arts Commission, for the graffiti-covered back wall of Folsom Playground; muralist Ray Patlan described a series of Native American images designed by twelve children, with a portrait of recreation director Jose Coronado.

At the request of Friends of Folsom Playground, and eight months after first deferring it, the Recreation and Park Commission renamed Folsom Playground "Jose Coronado Playground" in honor of its late recreation director.

After a final community meeting, the Recreation and Park Commission chose Scheme C, with a variation, for renovating Jose Coronado Playground: a community building with restrooms and the children's play area in the northeast part of the playground, with a soccer and softball area and basketball and tennis courts.
The Board of Supervisors bought the land at 21st and Folsom Streets for the Playground Commission's Folsom Playground.
